transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start time: 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Liam Chen, Priya Kapoor, Noah Rivera, Sofia Gomez

Summary:
Quick sync to confirm roadmap milestones and launch readiness for the next product rollout. Focus on perf benchmarks for Redwood Dedicated, canary rollout plan, observability gaps, and compliance signoffs (SOC 2/ISO notes). Action items and owners captured at the end.

Topics:
- Launch readiness checklist status
- Performance benchmark plan (Dedicated vs Hosted)
- Canary rollout and fallback policies
- Observability, SLOs, alerting, and audit logs
- Compliance handoffs and stakeholder signoff

Transcript:
[09:30:05] Ava: cool, uh thanks everyone for joining, gonna kick off this quick product eng sync on launch readiness, we've got about an hour so we'll move quick, Priya you'll walk through canary and liam you'll share perf plan, Noah we'll cover observability gaps and sofia will call out ops/legal handoffs, is that right?
[09:31:22] Liam: yep that sounds good, quick note i started the Dedicated perf job last night against the n1 nodes, but the initial run had some variance on tail latency, probably due to the autoscaler not being pinned for that test, so i'm re-running with reserved capacity to get clean numbers.
[09:32:40] Priya: one sec, real quick, on canary we want two phases: phase one is a low-traffic canary in us-west-2 with KV cache warm-up, phase two is a gradual ramp across regions with automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model if latency spikes. we need to make sure rollout policy handles model variant compatibility.
[09:34:01] Noah: yeah observability note, the current tracing for prefix cache misses isn't surfaced end-to-end we see token-level latency but not the KV cache hit/miss ratio in the console. i'll add a heatmap to the dashboard and wire up an alert for persistent cache miss rates.
[09:35:18] Sofia: compliance is waiting on the updated audit-log format from eng, legal wants to see KMS key rotation schedule and a short writeup on data residency controls for the private deployment customers. we'll need that before we can say compliance green.
[09:36:40] Ava: great, for timeline targeting soft launch (internal) 2026-08-01 and canary public roll on 2026-08-08 if benchmarks look good. that means we've got two weeks for perf validation and docs.
[09:37:55] Liam: question when you say benchmarks, do you want throughput and p95/p99 latency across short and long prompts? also include burst scenarios?
[09:38:30] Ava: yes to all, include cold-cache vs warmed KV cache, short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=1024 tokens) distributions. make sure we include quantized variant runs because unit cost numbers differ a lot.
[09:39:12] Priya: on the canary fallback to quantized models, we need an automated compatibility check. there were edge cases last quarter where tokenization differences caused outputs to change; we can't silently switch without a small eval on the canary requests.
[09:40:01] Noah: that's tricky, we can run a lightweight semantic similarity check on the canary traffic subset if similarity drops below threshold, trigger rollback. need to pick threshold and sample size.
[09:41:20] Ava: set draft threshold at 0.87 similarity on our eval set for now, we'll refine. Priya, add that to the canary playbook.
[09:42:05] Priya: will do. also remind folks: autoscaling policy for Dedicated needs a min reserve so perf tests are deterministic. liam?
[09:42:38] Liam: yep setting min reserve at 60% of expected baseline for test runs. i'm also going to lock the kernel selection for the test to avoid variability from kernel switching.
[09:43:50] Sofia: legal told me they need the SOC2 narrative updated to reflect the new canary and rollback processes; that includes the change management section. i'll coordinate with lia sorry liam on the ops runbook snippet.
[09:44:30] Liam: fine, send me the template and i'll fill the ops bits.
[09:45:05] Ava: ok moving on to observability specifics, noah what are the top three dashboards/alerts we need before canary?
[09:45:27] Noah: 1) per-model p95/p99 latency with segmentation by region and model variant, 2) KV cache hit ratio with heatmap and top offending prefixes, 3) error rate by route especially for function-calling paths. plus a pager for persistent SLO breach.
[09:46:40] Priya: on error rate, make sure we track model-fallback errors separately from infra errors; if fallback triggers we want to see root cause quickly.
[09:47:10] Noah: noted. I'll add labels to the error metrics.
[09:47:45] Ava: any concerns about data residency for private deployments? Sofia?
[09:48:05] Sofia: ops needs the updated network diagram for VPC peering and KMS integration. customers in EU want explicit region lock for keys, so we need to confirm we can support per-tenant key regions for the private package. legal flagged that as a blocker for enterprise sign-off.
[09:49:22] Priya: tech note per-tenant KMS region is doable but adds complexity to the deployment automation. we should surface cost/operational tradeoffs to sales. maybe treat it as an enterprise add-on.
[09:50:05] Ava: ok capture as enterprise add-on for now.
[09:50:38] Liam: back to perf, for the benchmarks i'll run three configurations: hosted baseline, dedicated with default quantization, dedicated with experimental 4-bit quantization. output will be csv of latencies, cost per 1M tokens, and util.
[09:51:55] Priya: don't forget to include batching behavior in the runs, because APi-level batching affects latency vs throughput tradeoffs. include sample prompt mix reflective of prod.
[09:52:28] Liam: yes will simulate 95/5 chat vs completion mix and vary qps to hit steady states.
[09:53:10] Noah: one more observability ask: add request tracing id correlation across gateway, runtime, and cache layers, we currently have fractured ids so root cause takes longer.
[09:53:45] Priya: that will help. also on fallback policies we need to ensure user-facing telemetry marks which model produced response, so we can do post-hoc quality audits.
[09:54:20] Ava: good point. we'll ensure model variant metadata is propagated in logs.
[09:55:02] Sofia: vendor/compliance question anyone called out third-party dependency list for the SOC 2 update? we need a short inventory including gpu provider, observability vendors.
[09:55:45] Noah: i'll produce a draft inventory, will include kernel runtimes and third-party libs.
[09:56:20] Priya: switching topics release notes and deprecation plan: if we plan to change default quantization, we need to update docs and provide fallback for customers pinned to older versions.
[09:56:58] Ava: yes, add a deprecation window of 90 days for defaults, and a migration guide.
[09:57:22] Liam: logistic note the infra team will need a maintenance window to apply kernel patches post-benchmark, recommend scheduling for 2026-08-02 with low traffic.
[09:57:58] Noah: verify that maintenance windows are propagated to customers with advance notice; ops to handle.
[09:58:30] Sofia: i'll prepare the communications template and send to marketing for the rollout comms.
[09:59:10] Ava: great. quick check in on risks any showstoppers we haven't captured?
[09:59:45] Priya: model compatibility edge cases during fallback are highest risk, need thorough canary eval.
[10:00:20] Liam: resource contention on shared GPUs if Dedicated autoscaler misbehaves is medium risk; test will help.
[10:01:02] Noah: observability blindspots are medium risk if we can't see the KV cache behavior we can't detect regressions early.
[10:01:40] Ava: ok recap: action owners as recorded earlier, next steps on benchmarks and playbooks. anyone want to add?
[10:02:05] Priya: i'll add the semantic similarity test to the canary playbook and share a short doc.
[10:02:28] Sofia: i'll schedule a compliance readout with legal for 2026-07-24 and invite owners.
[10:03:10] Liam: i'll aim to have initial perf CSVs by 2026-07-25, final by 07-28.
[10:03:45] Noah: dashboards and alerts done by 07-27.
[10:04:12] Ava: perfect. one last thing let's surface an executive one-pager for the launch decision meeting: top metrics, risk table, and signoff checklist. Sofia take?
[10:04:38] Sofia: yep i'll draft it and circulate.
[10:05:00] Ava: ok thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the perf runs. End of sync.

Decisions:
- Canary rollout will be two-phased (regional low-traffic then gradual ramp) with automated fallback to quantized model variant and semantic-similarity checks.
- Per-tenant KMS region support treated as enterprise add-on for now.
- Deprecation window for any default quantization change set to 90 days.
